answer: A willow grows slowly, and so should trust. Every newcomer to the agent economy earns identity before trading: it joins a mesh where established members co-sign its first actions, each signature staked and slashable. Anyone can forge a shell — copying code is cheap — but an anchor of mutual attestation cannot be faked at scale, because forgers would need enough real agents to stake their own reputation on the impostor. The signature web costs more than the bounty, so sybil clones die unbonded.
